question.problem:
Find the point(s) of the intersection of the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{6}=1$ and the line 
$\{\begin{aligned}x=t \\ y=1-t, \\ z=t+2\end{aligned}$ where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
question.worked_solution:
Substituting the expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ from the parametric equation of the line into the equation of the ellipsoid, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ 3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =6 \\ 3(t)^{2}+2(1-t)^{2}+(t+2)^{2} & =6 \\ 3{t}^{2}+2(1-2t+{t}^{2})+({t}^{2}+4t+4) & =6 \\ 6{t}^{2}+6 & =6 \\ 6{t}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solution $t=0.$ 

Now, we substitute our solution $t=0$ back into the equations of the line.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=0 \\ y=1-(0)=1 \\ z=(0)+2=2,\end{aligned}
$$

so the point is $(0,1,2).$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,1,2).$
